name: Blow a large bubble with bubble gum
blurb: A genuinely trivial skill with a real technique behind it: gum preparation, tongue position and slow steady air.
gear: Proper bubble gum, which has more elastic polymer than chewing gum
steps: Chew two or three pieces until the sugar is gone and the gum is smooth, soft and uniformly warm.
Flatten the gum against the roof of your mouth or your teeth into a thin, even disc.
Push the tip of your tongue into the centre of the disc to form a small pocket, keeping the edges sealed against your teeth and lips.
Blow slowly and steadily rather than hard — sudden pressure bursts the film.
Keep the bubble walls even by adjusting tongue and lip pressure as it grows.
Practise until you can go large without a face full of gum.
tips: Uneven thickness is why bubbles pop early. Spend longer flattening.
Cold gum will not stretch. Warm it up by chewing longer.
proof: A bubble wider than your face, three times in a row.
